queries.search_text: site:single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu 2025 late payments SMEs report invoice payment delays Europe official
queries.proposition: The European Commission reports that more than half of EU companies had late-payment difficulties in 2024, average B2B and government-to-business payment periods exceeded 60 days, larger buyers paid less reliably, and collection creates administrative burden; this supports a broad cash-flow and information-asymmetry problem but not demand for any proposed product.
queries.status: problem supported; willingness to pay and Poland-specific segment economics unproven
queries.contradiction: Payment performance varies materially by country and sector, and the source says transparency outcomes are not guaranteed because reporting can be heterogeneous, incomplete, unclear, and hard to access.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Interview ten Polish SME finance leads across the five proposed niches using anonymized overdue-invoice examples, then request a refundable paid pilot deposit from at least two for the specific intervention relevant to them.

queries.search_text: site:ure.gov.pl 2025 Poland negative electricity prices curtailment renewable energy flexible demand official report
queries.source_title: Prezes Urzędu Regulacji Energetyki publikuje Raport Krajowy za 2025 rok
queries.proposition: Poland's energy regulator reports distribution tariffs that accommodate flexibility services or dynamic-price customers, continued CSIRE rollout and interval-meter replacement, seven approved operator storage installations, and designated high-impact electricity-sector cybersecurity candidates; these create concrete operational transitions without proving buyer budgets.
queries.status: mechanism and regulatory transition supported; addressable customers, data access, savings, and willingness to pay unproven
queries.contradiction: The regulator also reports improving outage metrics and lower approved household tariffs, so urgency cannot be inferred from grid reliability or headline prices alone; flexibility participation and CSIRE access rules may constrain third parties.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Obtain three sample interval-data exports and conduct eight buyer interviews, then sell one fixed-fee shadow analysis that requires no automated switching or market participation.

concepts.title: Public-Invoice Acceptance Sentinel
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A pre-submission validator and timestamped evidence vault helps small suppliers prevent avoidable public-sector invoice rejection while the supplier, not the slow authority, pays for faster acceptance.
concepts.customer: Polish construction and medical-supply SMEs invoicing municipalities, hospitals, or other public bodies
concepts.loss_event: An invoice is rejected, disputed, or silently stalled because required acceptance evidence is missing or inconsistent, extending working-capital lockup.
concepts.beneficiary: Supplier treasury team and employees dependent on cash flow
concepts.risk_bearer: Supplier carrying payroll, tax, and materials costs until payment
concepts.transaction_owner: Platform operator owning validation workflow, evidence vault, and submission receipt
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed fee for validating and packaging one live invoice before submission
concepts.acquisition_route: Accountants refer clients with recurrent public invoices into a paid single-invoice trial.
concepts.compounding_asset: Anonymized rejection-reason taxonomy and buyer-specific document checklist library
hypotheses: Preventable acceptance errors contribute enough delay to justify a per-invoice fee.
Suppliers can lawfully upload the necessary contract and delivery metadata.
Accounting partners can acquire customers without long enterprise sales cycles.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not fabricate delivery evidence, impersonate an authorized approver, or represent validation as a guarantee of payment.

concepts.title: Milestone Evidence Escrow for Renovation Crews
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A neutral evidence-and-signoff workflow lets small renewable and renovation subcontractors convert disputed completion milestones into financeable receivables.
concepts.customer: Small photovoltaic, heat-pump, electrical, and retrofit subcontractors working under larger contractors
concepts.loss_event: The general contractor delays milestone approval, leaving the subcontractor unable to invoice or finance completed work.
concepts.beneficiary: Subcontractor and, secondarily, any receivables financier
concepts.authority_holder: Contractually named site supervisor or general-contractor representative
concepts.distributor: Renewable-equipment wholesalers and regional installer associations
concepts.risk_bearer: Subcontractor funding labor and materials before signoff
concepts.transaction_owner: Platform operator managing the agreed checklist, evidence trail, and signoff request
concepts.first_paid_event: A fee when one project milestone package is accepted or deemed ready for invoice submission
concepts.acquisition_route: Bundle a first project through wholesalers already extending trade credit to installers.
concepts.compounding_asset: Trade-specific milestone templates and anonymized signoff-cycle benchmarks by contractor
hypotheses: Ambiguous or incomplete milestone proof is a material source of payment delay.
General contractors will interact with a supplier-selected neutral workflow.
Evidence completeness improves receivables-finance eligibility.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not alter timestamps, invent completion records, or imply that platform evidence overrides the underlying contract.

concepts.title: Buyer Payment-Behavior Underwriting Feed
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: An opt-in ledger feed pools verified settlement timing from SME accounting systems so trade-credit brokers can price buyer concentration risk before invoices are issued.
concepts.customer: Trade-credit insurance brokers, invoice financiers, and accounting networks serving Polish SMEs
concepts.loss_event: A financier or supplier underprices exposure to a large buyer because recent payment behavior is opaque.
concepts.payer: Broker, financier, or accounting-network risk team
concepts.beneficiary: SME suppliers receiving better client selection and credit terms
concepts.authority_holder: Each contributing business controller authorizing use of its transaction data
concepts.risk_bearer: Financier or supplier exposed to delayed settlement
concepts.transaction_owner: Data cooperative operator controlling contribution rules and aggregated outputs
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid one-buyer risk report generated from consented contributors
concepts.acquisition_route: Recruit one accounting network as a data-and-distribution anchor and presell reports to its finance partners.
concepts.compounding_asset: Permissioned longitudinal payment-timing graph by buyer, sector, and invoice type
hypotheses: Accounting exports contain sufficiently consistent invoice and settlement fields.
A privacy-preserving aggregate remains predictive at useful coverage.
Risk teams will pay before the dataset reaches national scale.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not scrape private ledgers, expose identifiable contributors, or publish unsupported allegations about a buyer.

concepts.title: Invoice Dispute Triage Desk
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A structured AI intake separates correctable invoice defects from genuine commercial disputes and routes each case to accounting, negotiation, or licensed counsel for a paid case fee.
concepts.customer: Owner-managed wholesalers and service SMEs with recurring overdue invoices
concepts.loss_event: Staff repeatedly chase the wrong contact or escalate an invoice without resolving the actual blocker, consuming time while cash remains unpaid.
concepts.authority_holder: Creditor's designated finance officer; licensed counsel for reserved legal work
concepts.distributor: Bookkeepers, factoring brokers, and business associations
concepts.risk_bearer: Creditor retaining default and relationship risk
concepts.transaction_owner: Triage service owning intake, chronology, and referral workflow but not the underlying claim
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed fee for a documented triage and next-action pack on one overdue invoice
concepts.acquisition_route: Bookkeepers surface aged invoices and offer a one-case paid referral at month-end close.
concepts.compounding_asset: Outcome-labeled blocker taxonomy and resolution-path dataset
hypotheses: A meaningful share of collection effort is wasted because blocker types are misclassified.
Customers value an inexpensive case decision before hiring counsel.
Referral partners can preserve privilege and professional boundaries.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not practice law without authorization, threaten debtors, or claim recovery certainty.

concepts.title: Supplier-Funded Early-Payment Auction
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A large buyer exposes approved invoices to a reverse auction in which suppliers choose the smallest discount they will accept for a fixed early-payment pool.
concepts.customer: Large Polish buyers with many SME suppliers and approved but not-yet-due invoices
concepts.loss_event: Suppliers face expensive or unavailable working capital while buyers cannot efficiently allocate limited early-payment capacity.
concepts.payer: Participating supplier through a disclosed discount or platform fee
concepts.beneficiary: Winning suppliers receive early cash; buyer may strengthen supply continuity
concepts.authority_holder: Buyer's treasury team approving invoice eligibility and payment release
concepts.distributor: ERP implementation partners and procurement-finance advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: Buyer for payment execution and supplier for the accepted discount
concepts.transaction_owner: Auction operator administering bids and settlement instructions while the buyer remains payer of record
concepts.first_paid_event: Platform fee on the first approved invoice paid ahead of its contractual due date
concepts.acquisition_route: Run a manual, capped auction with one buyer's existing supplier portal and treasury team.
concepts.compounding_asset: Buyer-specific liquidity-demand curves and supplier participation history
hypotheses: Buyers hold usable early-payment liquidity but lack allocation tooling.
Supplier discounts beat their alternative financing cost.
Accounting and tax treatment permits a simple disclosed workflow.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not hide the effective financing cost, manipulate bids, or sell the same receivable twice.

concepts.title: Installer Flex-Readiness Certificate
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A white-label audit lets renewable installers prove whether an existing customer site has the metering, controllable loads, contract, and economics needed for dynamic pricing or flexibility services before selling hardware.
concepts.customer: Regional photovoltaic, heat-pump, battery, and EV-charger installers
concepts.loss_event: An installer spends sales and engineering time proposing storage or controls to a site that cannot access the necessary tariff, data, or controllable load.
concepts.payer: Installer or its prospective commercial customer
concepts.beneficiary: Installer sales team and site energy manager
concepts.authority_holder: Site owner plus relevant retailer or distribution-system operator for contract and grid matters
concepts.distributor: Renewable-equipment wholesalers and the founder's family installation network
concepts.risk_bearer: Installer if promised savings fail; site owner for investment performance
concepts.transaction_owner: Audit provider owning the assessment workflow while installer owns the equipment sale
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed-fee flex-readiness report for one commercial site
concepts.acquisition_route: Offer a white-label report to installers for stalled battery or controls proposals.
concepts.compounding_asset: Site archetype benchmarks linking load shape, tariff eligibility, controls, and realized project outcomes
hypotheses: Installers lose enough effort on unqualified flexibility leads to pay for screening.
Customers can export usable interval data.
A vendor-neutral report improves close rates without guaranteeing savings.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not guarantee savings, bypass retailer or operator rules, or treat simulated performance as measured fact.

concepts.title: Cold-Store Flex Dispatch Shadow Desk
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A read-only service converts interval prices and refrigeration constraints into next-day load-shift recommendations, letting a cold store verify savings before authorizing automation.
concepts.customer: Independent cold stores, food processors, and refrigerated warehouses with shiftable thermal load
concepts.loss_event: The operator consumes heavily in costly intervals or ignores potential flexibility because no one translates market signals into food-safe operating actions.
concepts.beneficiary: Facility owner; retailer or aggregator may later benefit from flexibility
concepts.authority_holder: Facility operations manager responsible for temperature and equipment limits
concepts.distributor: Industrial refrigeration service firms and energy advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: Facility owner bears spoilage, equipment, and bill risk
concepts.transaction_owner: Analytics provider owning recommendation delivery; facility retains dispatch control
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid four-week shadow report comparing recommended versus actual load timing
concepts.acquisition_route: Refrigeration technicians refer sites with interval meters for a no-control shadow pilot.
concepts.compounding_asset: Anonymized thermal-response and savings model by refrigeration configuration
hypotheses: A usable share of refrigeration demand can shift without affecting product safety.
Dynamic-price exposure or an aggregator contract makes timing economically relevant.
Shadow recommendations predict savings accurately enough to earn automation trust.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not control refrigeration during the proof phase or recommend actions outside documented food-safety and equipment limits.

concepts.title: Local Battery Evidence Broker
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A site-ranking service packages interval-load, outage, connection, land, and stakeholder evidence so municipalities or energy cooperatives can commission storage studies only where several beneficiaries align.
concepts.customer: Municipal utilities, energy cooperatives, renewable developers, and industrial parks
concepts.loss_event: Sponsors pay for engineering on battery sites where the grid need, host economics, land control, or approval path does not align.
concepts.beneficiary: Sponsor, local network users, and participating site hosts
concepts.authority_holder: Distribution-system operator and applicable permitting and land authorities
concepts.distributor: Grid consultants, regional installers, and municipal energy advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: Sponsor bears development spend and merchant revenue risk
concepts.transaction_owner: Evidence broker owning screening and data room; licensed engineers and developers own formal studies and delivery
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed-fee ranked shortlist and evidence data room for one municipality or industrial park
concepts.acquisition_route: Sell a bounded desktop screen before the sponsor commissions grid or engineering studies.
concepts.compounding_asset: Geospatial site library with observed approval, connection, and project outcomes
hypotheses: Early evidence can eliminate enough weak sites to justify the screening fee.
Relevant interval and connection information is obtainable lawfully.
Sponsors value neutral screening despite uncertain storage revenue.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not imply regulator or operator endorsement, promise a connection, or present screening as a licensed engineering study.

concepts.title: Energy Vendor Cyber Evidence Passport
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A reusable evidence passport lets small vendors answer recurring cybersecurity due-diligence requests from high-impact electricity entities without each buyer rebuilding the questionnaire.
concepts.customer: Small software, controls, metering, and maintenance vendors selling to electricity operators or other high-impact entities
concepts.loss_event: A vendor loses or delays a contract because it cannot assemble consistent, current evidence for buyer security review.
concepts.payer: Vendor CEO, security lead, or bid manager
concepts.beneficiary: Vendor sales team and buyer security reviewers
concepts.authority_holder: Each buyer's security and procurement functions, plus competent authorities for binding obligations
concepts.distributor: Energy procurement consultants, managed-security providers, and sector associations
concepts.risk_bearer: Vendor bears lost-deal and disclosure risk; buyer retains supply-chain cyber risk
concepts.transaction_owner: Passport provider controlling evidence collection, expiry tracking, and buyer-specific export
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid evidence-gap assessment and one buyer-ready response pack
concepts.acquisition_route: Partner with managed-security firms that discover documentation gaps during bids or renewals.
concepts.compounding_asset: Versioned control-to-evidence map and anonymized buyer-question taxonomy
hypotheses: Energy buyers repeatedly request overlapping control evidence from vendors.
Vendors will pay to shorten bid cycles before a formal audit is required.
Buyers accept structured exports while retaining independent review.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not issue a false certification, conceal control gaps, or claim that a passport replaces a buyer's required audit.
